finite_source_witnesses.kind: Finite source-derived schedules, order lists and arithmetic projections. No Java target calls or world fixtures.
finite_source_witnesses.clock_assumptions: Both cores registered/eligible and fully loaded from the first ordinary world tick, stable formed/powered network, world game time advances once per server step. Compare only steps21..60 to exclude original first-tick callback registration. Step j starts global old counter j-1; persisted modern game-time residue r is read after increment r+j. No first-frame, frozen-server, skipped-world or actual-restart claim.

logic_usage_projection.limit: Full success leaves original while preincrement counter at total+1, current counts successful operations. Only the two clamped display projections are accepted, not equality of raw saved counters/API values.

limits: No same-tick real energy/endpoint visibility, provider mutation, inter-core scheduling, throughput/TPS, client redstone or restart acceptance.59 positions are rank/channel dispatch, not59 real endpoints.
128EU reserve sufficiency is not generalized to foreign overstacked items or arbitrary handlers; prior quantity/return-policy findings remain.

policy_boundaries: Cadence is still every20 advancing ticks; altered phase is a scheduling contract difference, not evidence of reduced steady throughput or vanilla dimension desynchronization.
Do not restore the original full-success preincrement counter bug; current real-operation count has the same clamped CPU display at saturation.

The public routeNetworkOnce helper itself does not enforce a one-second gate. Current ordinary production calls it only through the normal server ticker; the comment now states that boundary accurately.
